heading: Only a minority of neuron explanations predict activations well, even from stronger explainers
definition: when neuron explanations are scored by simulating activations on new text, only a minority of neurons get good scores, even with stronger explainer models.
summary: Several independent groups report low average simulation scores (how well an explanation predicts activations) for neuron explanations on GPT-2 XL, small GPT-2 and CRATE (white-box transformer) models, and Gemma 2. Outside the original, only an informal 50-neuron post reproduces the finding that just a minority of neurons are well explained, and the evidence that stronger explainers still leave most neurons poorly scored is indirect.

suggested_status.by_scale: GPT-2 XL (the original's setting; size not stated in the rows): R2. Low means come from several non-original groups, but outside the original the share result comes only from an informal 50-neuron post. <1B: R2 from one independent study (arXiv:2410.16443, GPT-2/CRATE up to 12 layers, means only). 1-10B: R2 from one independent study on another family (arXiv:2502.12483, Gemma 2 2B/9B, means only). 10-100B and >100B: no test (counts: V7.studies_by_size has no such key). Toy: none.
suggested_status.reason:
Groups other than the original's report low simulation scores for neuron explanations (counts: V7.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 0).
- On GPT-2 XL random neurons, arXiv:2310.06200 reports means of 0.0962–0.1249, and arXiv:2610.37676 reports pooled r of 0.125–0.197. lw:drMv4SM2gaxk3oz3m finds 8% at the 0.8 criterion with Opus 5.5.
- On GPT-2 and CRATE models with 1–12 layers, arXiv:2410.16443 reports layer means of 1.37–14.2 (ρ in %). On another family, arXiv:2502.12483 reports means of 0.18 for Gemma 2 2B and 0.13 for 9B.
- Verdict counts: V7.verdicts.supports.studies 5, V7.verdicts.limits_scope.studies 1, V7.verdicts.challenges.studies 0.
Caveats:
- The 'minority share' itself is reproduced only by the informal LessWrong post. The others give means.
- arXiv:2610.37676 reuses the original's released GPT-4 explanations and scores.
- arXiv:2410.16443 has the one limits_scope verdict. In it, the simulator (Table 7: LLaMA-2-7B vs LLaMA-2-70B, GPT-3.5-turbo explainer) and the sequence set (Table 2: top-and-random vs random-only) move the scores. The authors say swapping the explainer (Mistral-7B vs GPT-3.5-turbo, Table 6) does not significantly change them.
- The evidence for the 'stronger explainer' part is indirect. lw:drMv4SM2gaxk3oz3m compares with GPT-4 by changing the explainer and the simulator together.
suggested_status.open_questions:
- A peer-reviewed, full-population result giving the share above a threshold, with a frontier explainer and simulator, on GPT-2 XL or a modern model.
- A test that changes only the explainer (simulator held fixed) and reports shares.
- Any test at 10B or above (counts: V7.studies_by_size has none), especially on the Qwen3-32B neurons from V1. If most neurons scored well there, V7 would be challenged.
- Whether pooled simulation scores reflect prediction at the token level. In arXiv:2610.37676, an explanation-free sequence-mean rule (0.288) beats GPT-4's simulator (0.160) on OpenAI's GPT-2 XL top-and-random sets.
- Whether refined pipelines such as NeuronScope (means up to 0.663; not a test) give majority shares above a stated threshold.

original_result.setup: GPT-4 wrote explanations for GPT-2 MLP neurons, then predicted each neuron's activations on held-out text from its explanation, and each explanation was scored by how well the predicted activations correlated with the real ones.
original_result.result: The average correlation score was 0.151 when tested on top-activating plus random text and 0.037 on random text only, and only 1.7% of GPT-2 XL neurons scored above 0.7 (0.2% on random text only). Scores rose smoothly with explainer capability, and human-written explanations scored better than GPT-4's but were still low in absolute terms.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: GPT-2 XL neurons averaged simulation scores near 0.10–0.12, even with GPT-4 and better prompts.
With Opus 5.5 explaining, only 8% of sampled GPT-2 XL neurons reached a 0.8 simulation score.
Explanations of GPT-2 and CRATE neurons predicted their activations weakly: layer-average correlation 1.4–14.2%.
Gemma 2 factual knowledge neurons averaged correlation 0.18 (smaller model) and 0.13 (larger); few scored well.
GPT-2 XL explanation scores stayed low; predicting each text's true mean activation beat all three simulators.
Replacing the 7B simulator with 70B raised some scores; low scores partly reflect 7B scoring models.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

No study scores their neuron explanations by simulation. The one large production model, Claude 3 Sonnet (arXiv:2605.29358), has no stated size and gets only a neurons-vs-features comparison.

wording_issues.phrase: only a minority of neurons get good scores
wording_issues.issue: Where shares are reported, they are a small fraction, not just a minority: 1.7% above 0.7 (top-and-random) and 0.2% (random-only) for GPT-4 on GPT-2 XL, and 8% at the 0.8 criterion (3–19% across criteria) for Opus 5.5 on 50 GPT-2 XL neurons. Every other test reports means, not shares: 0.0962–0.1249; pooled r 0.125–0.197; IS 0.18/0.13; 1.4–14.2 (ρ in %).

wording_issues.issue: No study changes only the explainer and reports a share, and the explainer-only results are mixed. The original reports scores improving smoothly with explainer capability, up to GPT-4 (R6). The LessWrong post changes explainer and simulator together (Opus 5.5 for both vs GPT-4 for both), plus the recipe (35 examples, multi-sentence explanations, direct 0–10 simulation). Opus beat GPT-4 on all 20 compared neurons (Opus mean 0.51 on those 20). Its appendix says the Opus simulator alone did better on GPT-4's explanations, and the combination was strongest. The fresh 30 neurons (mean 0.41) had no GPT-4 comparison. 8% reach 0.8 (criterion inferred), against the original's 0.3% for GPT-4 as the post cites it. Prompt Tuning (GPT-2 XL, GPT-3.5-Turbo-Instruct simulator, Table 2), Random neurons, GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5 explainer: Original prompt 0.1211 vs 0.0962, Highlight 0.1241 vs 0.1129, AVHS 0.1219 vs 0.1093, Summary 0.1238 vs 0.1249, HS 0.1193 vs 0.1239. On Random Interpretable neurons, GPT-3.5 is higher for every prompt (Original prompt: GPT-3.5 0.2420, GPT-4 0.2284). The neuron samples differ: 20 per layer for GPT-3.5, 10 for GPT-4. CRATE/GPT: the authors say swapping Mistral-7B for GPT-3.5-turbo as explainer does not significantly change scores (Table 6). Simulator choice also moves scores (method_sensitivity[1]), but the statement names only explainers.

wording_issues.phrase: scored by simulating activations on new text
wording_issues.issue: Which text is used changes the result. Original, GPT-2 XL with GPT-4: the share above 0.7 is 1.7% with top-and-random sequences and 0.2% with random-only. Scoring Explanations, on 49 GPT-2 small SAE features (not neurons): Jev's mean score falls from 0.478 on stored peak-centred crops to 0.331 on random-offset natural windows (44 of 49 lower). The two sets also differ in window length (17 vs 64 tokens) and composition, so the cause is not isolated. On OpenAI's 400 GPT-2 XL top-and-random sets, an explanation-free sequence-mean oracle (eta) reaches 0.288, above GPT-4 0.160, Jev 0.197 and Llama-3.1-8B 0.125. On the natural windows of the 49 features, Jev 0.331 is above eta 0.166. The paper concludes that a pooled score alone cannot show token-level skill, and that Jev's lead over GPT-4 is mostly between sequences. Scores still depend on the explanation: Jev with shuffled explanations drops to 0.017, and GPT-4's simulator did not see sequence order. Knowledge Microscope scores on 6 held-out factual-triple samples, not free text.

method_sensitivity.what: With explanations held fixed on 400 GPT-2 XL neurons, mean pooled r is 0.125 for Llama-3.1-8B, 0.160 for GPT-4 (published) and 0.197 for Jev. In CRATE/GPT, a 70B simulator raises GPT-1L from 9.0 to 13.4 (ρ in %; from the verdict's reading of Table 7). The LessWrong post's missing line says Opus 5.5 simulating GPT-4's explanations did better than GPT-4 (no numbers in rows).

method_sensitivity.factor: Explainer model and prompt format (the LessWrong comparison swaps the whole pipeline)
method_sensitivity.what: Prompt Tuning (GPT-2 XL random neurons, GPT-3.5-Turbo-Instruct simulator; 20 neurons per layer for the GPT-3.5 explainer, 10 for GPT-4): with the Original prompt, the GPT-3.5 explainer scores 0.0962 and GPT-4 0.1211. With the Summary prompt they score 0.1249 and 0.1238. The authors report that GPT-3.5 favours Summary while GPT-4 is more similar across prompts. The original reports smooth gains with explainer capability. In CRATE, GPT-3.5-turbo is similar to Mistral-7B as explainer (verdict, from Table 6). The LessWrong post changes the whole pipeline, not the explainer alone: Opus 5.5 as explainer and simulator (35 examples, multi-sentence explanations, direct 0–10 simulation) beat GPT-4 as explainer and simulator on all 20 neurons compared. Its appendix says the Opus simulator alone improved on GPT-4's explanations, and the combination had the strongest effect.

method_sensitivity.what: Scoring Explanations. On 49 GPT-2 small SAE features (not neurons), Jev's mean simulation score is 0.478 on stored peak-centred crops and 0.331 on random-offset natural windows (44 of 49 lower). The two sets also differ in window length (17 vs 64 tokens) and composition, which are not tested separately; 74-token stitched passages keep 0.476, a partial control for length only. On OpenAI's top-and-random sets for 400 GPT-2 XL neurons, an explanation-free sequence-mean oracle reaches pooled r 0.288, above GPT-4's 0.160, Jev's 0.197 and Llama-3.1-8B's 0.125. On the natural windows of the 49 features, Jev (0.331) is above the oracle (0.166). Sequence order is a cue: a post hoc explanation-free rule that predicts activity on the first five (top-activating) sequences of OpenAI's release scores 0.227. GPT-4's simulator did not see the order.

LessWrong post, Opus 5.5 on GPT-2 XL layers 8–40: the mean score is 0.51 on the first 20 neurons, on which the pipeline was developed, and 0.41 on a fresh 30. The post also reports a slight drop in simulator score when 12 neurons were batched (method-sensitivity line).

Original: explainability trends downward with subject size across GPT-3-series models from 98K to 6.7B. Its method-sensitivity line also lists layer, activation function (ReLU beats GeLU) and activation statistics. Knowledge Microscope: mean IS is 0.18 for Gemma 2 2B and 0.13 for 9B. N2G (graph-based firing prediction, no V7 verdict): firing-token F1 is 0.74 at layer 0, 0.64 at layer 1 and 0.6 at layer 2 in a six-layer SoLU model. CRATE reports that scores vary with depth.

method_sensitivity.what: Neurons vs dictionary features, each study scoring both units with one simulation protocol; relative results only. In Claude 3 Sonnet, with Claude 3 Opus explaining 100 random neurons and 100 random features, the neurons were significantly less interpretable. In a small model, neuron scores were lower than feature scores. In the Pythia-70M MLP sublayer (model inferred from context; Appendix C.3, Fig. 10), the authors call the result mixed success: many SAE features were more interpretable than the neurons, but the SAE learned many dead features except in early layers. Neuron scores are figure-only, with no average comparison in the text. All these rows are cannot_determine for V7 and give no absolute shares; none of these studies has a V7 verdict.

method_sensitivity.factor: Explanation pipeline (multi-agent refinement, fine-tuned simulator); from a study marked not a test
method_sensitivity.what: NeuronScope reports mean neuron-level Pearson scores over 200 neurons, its own method against its own ablation. At layer 5: Llama-3.1-8b 0.453 without refinement and 0.508 with it; Gemma-2-2b 0.600 and 0.663; Qwen3-4b 0.489 and 0.589. At layer 10, Llama-3.1-8b scores 0.334 and 0.390. These means are far above the 0.13–0.18 Gemma 2 means elsewhere, but the study is not a test of V7 and gives no shares. Use for coverage only.
